title: Pandemic Tracking and the Future of Data

sentences.en: This episode is one in a four part series that we're calling the future of dot dot dot.
sentences.zh: 本期节目是我们称之为“……的未来”的四集系列节目之一。

sentences.en: We'll be exploring how changes of the way we live, learn, work and play may shape our health and well-being in years to come.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨生活、学习、工作和娱乐方式的改变将如何在未来几年塑造我们的健康与福祉。

sentences.en: Thanks to the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation for supporting this episode.
sentences.zh: 感谢罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会对本期节目的支持。

sentences.en: The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation is committed to improving health and health equity in the United States.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会致力于改善美国的健康与健康公平。

sentences.en: Learn more about them at rwjf.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问 rwjf.org 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: Hey, producer Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 嘿，制作人德兰妮·霍尔。

sentences.en: So you're here with the next story in our series called the future of dot dot dot.
sentences.zh: 所以你带着我们系列节目中的下一个故事来到了这里，这个系列叫“……的未来”。

sentences.en: And you're here to talk about the future of data.
sentences.zh: 你是来谈论数据未来的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And I feel like I should just level with you and our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我应该对你和我们的听众开诚布公。

sentences.en: This is a story about spreadsheets.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于电子表格的故事。

sentences.en: OK, it's a story about spreadsheets and data entry and data systeMs.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个关于电子表格、数据输入和数据系统的故事。

sentences.en: A story about spreadsheets.
sentences.zh: 一个关于电子表格的故事。

sentences.en: It's not even my birthday, Delaney.
sentences.zh: 今天甚至都不是我的生日，德兰妮。

sentences.en: How do I get this marvelous gift?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能得到这份美妙的礼物？

sentences.en: I should have known I wouldn't have to convince you.
sentences.zh: 我早该知道我不必说服你。

sentences.en: You do not have to convince me.
sentences.zh: 你根本不用说服我。

sentences.en: I'm already riveted.
sentences.zh: 我已经听得入迷了。

sentences.en: So let's go.
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧。

sentences.en: OK, so we'll start in the early days of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将从大流行的早期开始。

sentences.en: Today, the entire city of Wuhan is on lockdown.
sentences.zh: 今天，整个武汉市都处于封锁状态。

sentences.en: And as COVID spread in Asia and then in other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 随着新冠疫情在亚洲蔓延，随后又扩散到世界其他地区。

sentences.en: The most active hotspot right now is Italy.
sentences.zh: 目前最活跃的热点地区是意大利。

sentences.en: Nearly.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: You are seeing officials take these wildly unprecedented steps to control the disease.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到官员们正在采取这些极其前所未有的措施来控制疫情。

sentences.en: Lockdowns.
sentences.zh: 封锁。

sentences.en: Quarantines.
sentences.zh: 隔离。

sentences.en: Massive amounts of testing.
sentences.zh: 大规模检测。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people thought we'd see the same kind of response in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都以为，当病毒传到美国时，

sentences.en: when the virus arrived here.
sentences.zh: 我们也会看到同样的应对反应。

sentences.en: You know, as someone who grew up reading The Hot Zone, I expected that we had the world's
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为一个从小读《血疫》长大的人，我曾以为我们拥有世界上

sentences.en: foremost infectious disease-fighting agency in the world.
sentences.zh: 最顶尖的传染病防治机构。

sentences.en: This is Alexis Madrigal.
sentences.zh: 这是亚历西斯·马德里加尔。

sentences.en: At the time the pandemic started, he was a journalist at The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 大流行开始时，他是《大西洋月刊》的一名记者。

sentences.en: And he's still a contributing writer there.
sentences.zh: 他现在仍然是那里的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: So I was expecting to see the United States of America assume global leadership and come
sentences.zh: 所以我当时期待看到美利坚合众国承担起全球领导责任，并想出

sentences.en: up with ways for us to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 应对疫情的办法。

sentences.en: And like Alexis, I was basically imagining scenes from outbreak and contagion in my head.
sentences.zh: 和亚历西斯一样，我脑海中基本上浮现的是电影《极度恐慌》和《传染病》里的场景。

sentences.en: You know, like brave epidemiologists in hazmat suits working with the best technology available
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如穿着防护服的勇敢流行病学家，利用手头最好的技术

sentences.en: to get a scary situation under control.
sentences.zh: 来控制可怕的局面。

sentences.en: And so, of course, we all wanted that to be the reality.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，我们都希望这能成为现实。

sentences.en: We all wanted that to be what our pandemic response looked like.
sentences.zh: 我们都希望这就是我们应对大流行时的样子。

sentences.en: Here's Robinson Meyer, Alexis's colleague at The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 这位是罗宾逊·迈耶，亚历西斯在《大西洋月刊》的同事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The CDC seemed like the last bastion of like absolutely competent American technocracy.
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心看起来就像是绝对称职的美国技术官僚主义的最后堡垒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Like they were on top of it.
sentences.zh: 就像他们完全掌控了局势一样。

sentences.en: But as we started to see cases of COVID here in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 但随着我们在美国开始看到新冠病例出现，

sentences.en: Alexis and Rob felt like the response from our public health agencies was surprisingly muted.
sentences.zh: 亚历西斯和罗布觉得，我们公共卫生机构的反应出奇地沉默。

sentences.en: We were not seeing mass testing like was happening in Asian countries.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到像亚洲国家那样的大规模检测。

sentences.en: And in fact, when they started looking, it was hard to find any concrete numbers at all about
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他们开始寻找时，很难找到任何关于

sentences.en: how much testing was happening here, which was not good because testing was the most crucial
sentences.zh: 这里到底进行了多少检测的具体数字，这可不是什么好事，因为检测是我们此时理解

sentences.en: data point that we had for understanding the pandemic at this point.
sentences.zh: 这场大流行最关键的数据点。

sentences.en: So I guess the CDC was not tracking that at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我想美国疾控中心当时并没有在追踪这些。

sentences.en: Well, at first it was.
sentences.zh: 嗯，起初是有的。

sentences.en: But then in early March 2020, the agency stopped reporting the total number of nationwide tests.
sentences.zh: 但随后在2020年3月初，该机构停止了报告全国检测总数。

sentences.en: And basically, they said most testing is happening at the state level.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们说大多数检测都是在州一级进行的。

sentences.en: So if you want to know, go ask the states.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想知道，去问各州吧。

sentences.en: The CDC just wasn't saying.
sentences.zh: 美国疾控中心就是不说。

sentences.en: So I was like, fine, we're going to go to the states.
sentences.zh: 所以我就想，好吧，那我们就去找各州。

sentences.en: So they reached out to all the states and asked some really basic questions.
sentences.zh: 于是他们联系了所有州，并问了一些非常基本的问题。

sentences.en: You know, how many people have you tested?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们检测了多少人？

sentences.en: How many positive cases have you had?
sentences.zh: 你们有多少阳性病例？

sentences.en: And how many tests can you do each day?
sentences.zh: 你们每天能做多少次检测？

sentences.en: And they were shocked by what they found.
sentences.zh: 而他们发现的结果让他们大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Oh, man, we tested almost nobody.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们几乎谁都没测。

sentences.en: And so what's that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: Almost nobody.
sentences.zh: 几乎谁都没测。

sentences.en: Like, what are the numbers for almost nobody?
sentences.zh: 比如说，“几乎谁都没测”具体的数字是多少？

sentences.en: Well, on March 6th, which was just a few days after the CDC stopped reporting testing numbers,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在3月6日——就在美国疾控中心停止报告检测数据的几天后，

sentences.en: Rob and Alexis could only verify that 1,895 people nationwide had been tested for COVID.
sentences.zh: 罗布和亚历西斯只能核实到全国仅有1895人接受了新冠病毒检测。

sentences.en: Even though the White House was saying that tens or hundreds of thousands of people could be tested per day by that point.
sentences.zh: 尽管白宫当时声称，到那时每天可以检测数万甚至数十万人。

sentences.en: So I do remember some of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实记得其中的一些情况。

sentences.en: There was this huge shortage of tests for hospitals to use at the beginning of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 大流行刚开始时，医院使用的检测工具严重短缺。

sentences.en: And there were pretty strict rules by the CDC about who could get tested at all because, you know, those tests were in short supply.
sentences.zh: 而且美国疾控中心对谁可以接受检测有着非常严格的规定，因为你知道，那些检测物资很短缺。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that ended up having enormous implications because without much testing, it was hard to know what was happening on the ground.
sentences.zh: 这最终产生了巨大的影响，因为如果没有进行大量检测，就很难了解实际情况。

sentences.en: If you looked at the state of the data, there was no data.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看数据的状态，就会发现根本没有数据。

sentences.en: And many states could test a dozen people a day.
sentences.zh: 许多州一天只能检测十几个人。

sentences.en: If the virus was circulating, we had no way to know.
sentences.zh: 如果病毒在传播，我们根本无从知晓。

sentences.en: And Alexis and Rob felt like they had wandered into this weird twilight zone where people at the top of our public health agencies were talking about carrying out a data-driven pandemic response,
sentences.zh: 亚历西斯和罗布觉得他们好像走入了一个奇怪的迷失地带，公共卫生机构的高层们口口声声说要开展数据驱动的抗疫行动，

sentences.en: but without actually having much data.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并没有多少数据。

sentences.en: And you'd be like, well, it seems like the virus could be everywhere then.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，那看来病毒可能无处不在了。

sentences.en: And they'd be like, well, the data doesn't say it is.
sentences.zh: 而他们会说，嗯，数据并没有显示是这样的。

sentences.en: But the data was s**t.
sentences.zh: 但那些数据简直是狗屁。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just the testing data that was limited.
sentences.zh: 而且受限制的不仅仅是检测数据。

sentences.en: It was also hard to find numbers on how many people were hospitalized and how many people had died.
sentences.zh: 也很难找到关于住院人数和死亡人数的统计数字。

sentences.en: And so Rob and Alexis decided to team up with a guy named Jeff Hammerbacher.
sentences.zh: 于是罗布和亚历西斯决定和一个叫杰夫·汉默巴赫的人合作。

sentences.en: He's a scientist and software developer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位科学家兼软件开发人员。

sentences.en: And they started compiling their own nationwide data sets based on what states were publishing.
sentences.zh: 他们开始根据各州公布的数据，整理他们自己的全国数据集。

sentences.en: And they thought of this as a stopgap.
sentences.zh: 他们把这视为一种权宜之计。

sentences.en: These are not fancy things, right?
sentences.zh: 这些可不是什么高深的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Cases, hospitalizations, deaths, number of tests performed.
sentences.zh: 病例、住院人数、死亡人数、检测数量。

sentences.en: Like, this is basic stuff.
sentences.zh: 听着，这都是些基础的东西。

sentences.en: Like, you look around the world and, like, all these other places just, like, have this stuff, you know?
sentences.zh: 你看世界各地，所有这些其他地方都有这些东西，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So we were just like, well, obviously, we'll also soon have this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时就想，好吧，显然我们很快也会拥有这些东西。

sentences.en: Because how could you run a public health response without good data?
sentences.zh: 因为没有好的数据，你怎么能开展公共卫生应对工作呢？

sentences.en: It's like the lifeblood of public health.
sentences.zh: 这就像是公共行业的生命线。

sentences.en: And it has been since the beginning of the field.
sentences.zh: 而且从这个领域诞生之初就是如此。

sentences.en: Okay, before we continue with the saga of Rob and Alexis, I want to tell you about some of that early public health history.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在我们继续讲述罗布和亚历西斯的故事之前，我想给你们讲讲早期公共卫生历史的一些内容。

sentences.en: Because some of it's fun.
sentences.zh: 因为其中有些部分挺有趣的。

sentences.en: Honestly, that's a big reason.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这占了很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: But also because it shows why data is so important and why our system makes it so hard to collect.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为这表明了为什么数据如此重要，以及为什么我们的体制让收集数据变得如此艰难。

sentences.en: Okay, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so there were many innovators in the realm of health data.
sentences.zh: 好的，健康数据领域曾有过许多创新者。

sentences.en: You know, people like Jon Snow, William Farr, W.E.B.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如约翰·斯诺、威廉·法尔、W·E·B·

sentences.en: Du Bois.
sentences.zh: 杜波依斯。

sentences.en: But I'm going to zoom in on one of the earliest examples.
sentences.zh: 但我打算聚焦于其中最早的例子之一。

sentences.en: We'll start with Jon Grant and the bills of mortality.
sentences.zh: 我们从约翰·格兰特和死亡统计清单开始讲起。

sentences.en: The bills of mortality.
sentences.zh: 死亡统计清单。

sentences.en: I like this.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: This is very ominous.
sentences.zh: 听起来很不祥。

sentences.en: I like it already.
sentences.zh: 我可太喜欢了。

sentences.en: So the bills of mortality were these mortality reports that were published in London in the 1600s.
sentences.zh: 死亡统计清单是17世纪在伦敦出版的死亡报告。

sentences.en: And every week, a group of parish clerks would gather and share information about who had died in the neighborhood and how.
sentences.zh: 每周，一群教区文书都会聚在一起，分享关于邻里间谁死了以及怎么死的信息。

sentences.en: And people would read them and they would kind of pick up the local parish thing and be like, oh, you know, Jon died.
sentences.zh: 人们会阅读这些清单，翻看当地教区的事，然后会说，哦，你知道吗，约翰死了。

sentences.en: So this is Stephen Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这位是斯蒂芬·约翰逊。

sentences.en: He wrote a book called Extra Life, A Short History of Living Longer.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本书，名叫《多活几年：长寿简史》。

sentences.en: And he says the bills were a source of fascination for many people.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些死亡清单曾让许多人着迷。

sentences.en: People liked to gossip about them.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢八卦上面的内容。

sentences.en: But they weren't what you would call structured data.
sentences.zh: 但它们算不上你所说的结构化数据。

sentences.en: Like there wasn't a way to detect useful patterns in the information there.
sentences.zh: 因为没法从中发现有用的模式信息。

sentences.en: But then Jon Grant comes along.
sentences.zh: 但随后约翰·格兰特出现了。

sentences.en: And Grant was a haberdasher slash amateur demographer.
sentences.zh: 格兰特是个杂货商兼业余人口统计学家。

sentences.en: That's a very 1600s combination of interests.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常17世纪风格的兴趣组合。

sentences.en: Yeah, you don't really get that kind of mix anymore.
sentences.zh: 是的，现在你很难再见到这种组合了。

sentences.en: So he was a classic kind of engaged amateur.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个典型的热心业余爱好者。

sentences.en: And he looked at the bills of mortality and thought there is more to be learned from these documents.
sentences.zh: 他查看了死亡统计清单，认为从这些文件中还能学到更多东西。

sentences.en: And so it occurred to him at some point in the early 1660s that if you try to assemble that data and look at it systematically,
sentences.zh: 于是在17世纪60年代初的某个时候，他突然意识到，如果你试图将这些数据汇集起来并系统地观察它们，

sentences.en: that you might be able to tell a lot more about what was really happening to the health of Londoners.
sentences.zh: 你或许就能更多地了解伦敦居民的健康状况究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: And so he spent all this time going from kind of parish to parish and reading through all these reports
sentences.zh: 于是他花了很多时间从一个教区走到另一个教区，阅读所有这些报告，

sentences.en: and kind of tabulating basically the data and trying to organize it in a more structured way.
sentences.zh: 并基本上将数据制成表格，试图以更有结构的方式将其组织起来。

sentences.en: And Grant ended up publishing a pamphlet with a very catchy title.
sentences.zh: 格兰特最终出版了一本小册子，书名非常吸引人。

sentences.en: It was called Natural and Political Observations Mentioned in a Following Index and Made Upon the Bills of Mortality.
sentences.zh: 它叫做《对死亡统计清单提及并依据随附索引做出的自然与政治观察》。

sentences.en: And what it enables both Grant to do but also health officials around the city is to suddenly be able to answer the question,
sentences.zh: 这不仅让格兰特，也让全城的卫生官员能够突然回答这样一个问题：

sentences.en: what is really killing people?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么在真正夺走人们的生命？

sentences.en: You know, where are the real threats?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，真正的威胁在哪里？

sentences.en: And how are those threats changing over time?
sentences.zh: 这些威胁又是如何随时间改变的？

sentences.en: Grant's work represented a huge conceptual breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 格兰特的工作代表了一次巨大的概念突破。

sentences.en: His pamphlet was basically the founding document of medical statistics and public health data.
sentences.zh: 他的这本小册子基本上是医学统计学和公共卫生数据的开山之作。

sentences.en: But it ultimately wasn't that useful because there was still a limited understanding of what was actually killing people.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，它并没有那么大用处，因为当时人们对究竟是什么在夺走生命仍有局限的理解。

sentences.en: For example, let me share with you the causes of death tabulated in this report.
sentences.zh: 例如，让我和你们分享一下这份报告中制成表格的死因。

sentences.en: The list is really pretty funny.
sentences.zh: 这个清单实际上相当滑稽。

sentences.en: According to Grant in 1662, about 1,300 people in London died of apoplex.
sentences.zh: 根据格兰特在1662年的记录，伦敦大约有1300人死于中风。

sentences.en: 38 died of cut of the stone.
sentences.zh: 38人死于切除结石手术。

sentences.en: 74 died of falling sickness.
sentences.zh: 74人死于癫痫。

sentences.en: 243 died of dead in the streets.
sentences.zh: 243人死于横死街头。

sentences.en: Only six died of leprosy, actually, which seems like you would have expected more in 1662.
sentences.zh: 说实话，只有六个人死于麻风病，在1662年这似乎比你预期的要多。

sentences.en: 158 died of lunatic.
sentences.zh: 158人死于精神失常。

sentences.en: And then my favorite category, 454, died of suddenly.
sentences.zh: 然后是我最喜欢的分类，454，死于突然。

sentences.en: Suddenly.
sentences.zh: 突然。

sentences.en: You can totally imagine the scenario where you get the answer suddenly.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以想象那种突然得到答案的场景。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，你问某个官员，他走过来问，他是怎么死的？

sentences.en: Others combined electronic submissions and faxed submissions.
sentences.zh: 其他州则结合了电子提交和传真提交。

sentences.en: But because people had to enter the faxed information to their tallies manually,
sentences.zh: 但由于人们必须将传真信息手动输入到他们的统计中，

sentences.en: there would be these big distortions in the data where all of a sudden a backlog of faxed results would just be dumped into the numbers all at once.
sentences.zh: 数据中就会出现巨大的偏差，积压的传真结果会突然一次性全部涌入数据中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You hold all the faxed ones to the end and then you enter them and then all of a sudden the numbers leap.
sentences.zh: 你把所有传真的结果留到最后，然后把它们输进去，接着数字就突然暴增了。

sentences.en: And it makes people mistrust data is what it does.
sentences.zh: 这导致人们对数据产生不信任，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: Or here's another example.
sentences.zh: 或者还有另一个例子。

sentences.en: When there would be a bad surge somewhere and lots of deaths, the people who fill out death certificates would get really behind.
sentences.zh: 当某个地方出现严重的疫情激增并导致大量死亡时，填写死亡证明的人就会严重滞后。

sentences.en: And so death numbers would lag.
sentences.zh: 因此死亡人数就会滞后。

sentences.en: Or yet another example, really critical demographic data would just be missing.
sentences.zh: 或者再举个例子，真正关键的人口统计数据竟然会缺失。

sentences.en: There really were whole areas, especially race and ethnicity, where most states and territories never developed a really robust way to collect that kind of demographic data.
sentences.zh: 确实有整个领域，尤其是种族和族裔方面，大多数州和领地从未开发出真正健全的方法来收集那类人口统计数据。

sentences.en: And when they did, it wasn't standardized.
sentences.zh: 即便他们收集了，也没有标准化。

sentences.en: Which, of course, meant it was hard to tell who was being most impacted by the disease.
sentences.zh: 这当然意味着很难判断谁受这种疾病的影响最大。

sentences.en: And this stuff can feel kind of dry, like ultimately we're talking about spreadsheets and data standardization.
sentences.zh: 这些内容可能会让人觉得有些枯燥，毕竟我们谈论的是电子表格和数据标准化。

sentences.en: But there was stuff going on at this time, early in the pandemic, where really good data could have helped.
sentences.zh: 但在大流行初期，当时确实有一些情况，如果能有真正优质的数据本可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: But these N95 respirator masks in particular are in high demand and short supply.
sentences.zh: 但特别是这些 N95 防护口罩，当时需求量极大且供应短缺。

sentences.en: Remember, for example, there was a massive shortage of protective gear for health care workers.
sentences.zh: 比方说，还记得医护人员的防护装备严重短缺吗？

sentences.en: But still, I have spoken to health care workers in San Francisco, Oakland, and San Jose today, all who say the shortage of supplies in their hospitals is a problem.
sentences.zh: 不过，我今天仍然与旧金山、奥克兰和圣何塞的医护人员交谈过，他们都表示医院物资短缺是一个问题。

sentences.en: If we had had the hospitalization data, knowing who had PPE, who had access to, you know, medications, who had staffing shortages, the federal government can, in fact,
sentences.zh: 如果我们有住院数据，知道谁有个人防护装备，谁能获得，你知道的，药物，谁有人手短缺，那么联邦政府实际上就可以

sentences.en: step in and help with that stuff.
sentences.zh: 介入并提供帮助。

sentences.en: Instead, that became this weird, crazy scramble that benefited nobody, as far as I can tell.
sentences.zh: 相反，那变成了一场奇怪、疯狂的争夺战，据我所知对任何人都没有好处。

sentences.en: So was the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以美国

sentences.en: government doing this type of data collection from the states and just not reporting it?
sentences.zh: 政府当时在从各州收集这类数据却只是不予报告？

sentences.en: Or were they just not doing it at all?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们根本就没做？

sentences.en: Well, in those early days, the people at the COVID Tracking Project certainly thought that the government had its own comprehensive numbers.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在早期，新冠追踪项目的成员当然认为政府有自己的综合数据。

sentences.en: They thought that someone somewhere within the vast CDC bureaucracy had stats and, you know, better stats than they did.
sentences.zh: 他们认为庞大疾病控制与预防中心官僚机构中的某个人在某处拥有统计数据，而且，你知道的，比他们拥有的统计数据更好。

sentences.en: I think all of us really thought that the data did exist, and we just couldn't see it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们所有人真的都认为数据是存在的，只是我们看不到罢了。

sentences.en: So the work that we were all doing was a stopgap.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所有人当时做的工作只是一种权宜之计。

sentences.en: And presumably, we would need to do it for a little while until the federal government released the numbers they had.
sentences.zh: 据推测，我们只需要做一段时间，直到联邦政府公布他们拥有的数据。

sentences.en: But then they started noticing some weird coincidences.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们开始注意到一些奇怪的巧合。

sentences.en: So this would have been in March and April 2020.
sentences.zh: 这大约发生在 2020 年 3 月和 4 月。

sentences.en: And back then, there were these press conferences that Vice President Mike Pence was doing.
sentences.zh: 当时副总统迈克·彭斯正在举行这些新闻发布会。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，总统先生。

sentences.en: And let me echo your words about all the dedicated men and women on the White House Coronavirus Task Force.
sentences.zh: 我要呼应你对白宫冠状病毒工作组所有敬业的男女同仁的赞赏。

sentences.en: And the COVID tracking people would watch those press conferences to see what kind of numbers the government shared
sentences.zh: 新冠追踪项目的人会观看这些新闻发布会，看看政府分享了什么样的数据，

sentences.en: and how they compared to the numbers that they were gathering.
sentences.zh: 以及它们与他们正在收集的数据相比如何。

sentences.en: It was reported to us that at this moment, more than 746,000 Americans have tested positive for the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 据向我们报告，目前已有超过 746,000 名美国人被检测出冠状病毒呈阳性。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, more than 68,000 Americans have fully recovered.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，已有超过 68,000 名美国人完全康复。

sentences.en: But sadly, more than 41,000 Americans have lost their lives to the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 但令人痛心的是，已有超过 41,000 名美国人因冠状病毒失去了生命。

sentences.en: And we were like, hey, you know, these numbers are really close to ours.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，嘿，你知道的，这些数字和我们的非常接近。

sentences.en: We must be doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 我们一定做得很好。

sentences.en: Because he's getting those federal numbers, clearly.
sentences.zh: 因为他显然拿到了联邦的数据。

sentences.en: And, you know, here we are just scraping from public data.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们在这里只是从公开数据中搜集。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that there have been more than 843,000 Americans who contracted the coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 尽管已有超过 843,000 名美国人感染了冠状病毒，

sentences.en: and we grieve the loss of more than 47,000 of our countrymen.
sentences.zh: 我们为失去超过 47,000 名同胞而感到悲痛。

sentences.en: And then we realized they were tracking really closely.
sentences.zh: 然后我们意识到他们的追踪结果非常吻合。

sentences.en: And I think a few of us started to suspect at that point that he was actually reading our numbers just rounded.
sentences.zh: 我想我们中的一些人当时开始怀疑他实际上是在阅读我们的数据并进行了四舍五入。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And then their suspicions were later confirmed when the Trump administration published a report that clearly used the project's data and charts and cited them in the footnotes.
sentences.zh: 后来，当特朗普政府发布了一份明显使用了该项目的 数据和图表并在脚注中引用它们的报告时，他们的怀疑得到了证实。

sentences.en: And it was like, oh, they're just looking at our site.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就像是，哦，他们只是在看我们的网站。

sentences.en: Like, we are the process.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们就是这个流程。

sentences.en: We are the ones who are making this data.
sentences.zh: 我们才是制造这些数据的人。

sentences.en: We were waiting for the cavalry, and then it turned out, like, we were the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在等待骑兵救援，结果发现，原来我们自己就是骑兵。

sentences.en: And we were like, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: We don't even have horses.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至连马都没有。

sentences.en: We can't be the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能是骑兵。

sentences.en: And it's kind of darkly funny, but it is also scary.
sentences.zh: 这有点黑色幽默，但同时也让人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: You know, you kind of think sometimes, like, well, you know, if Disaster X were to happen, well, you know, somebody's thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时你可能会想，嗯，你知道的，如果灾难 X 发生的话，好吧，你知道的，会有人在考虑这个。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, well, somebody's going to do that.
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，总有人会去做的。

sentences.en: And the truth is, no.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，并没有。

sentences.en: Nobody's going to f***ing do it sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时候根本没有人他妈的去做。

sentences.en: We were not ready.
sentences.zh: 我们没有准备好。

sentences.en: We did not have a system in place.
sentences.zh: 我们没有建立相应的系统。

sentences.en: And so I can imagine them feeling panicked about, like, oh, my God, okay, so we thought we were just messing around.
sentences.zh: 所以我能想象他们当时有多恐慌，比如，天哪，好吧，我们以为我们只是在瞎搞。

sentences.en: We're doing our beSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在尽最大努力。

sentences.en: And we thought that the government was going to save us, and it turned out they're not.
sentences.zh: 我们以为政府会来拯救我们，结果发现他们并没有。

sentences.en: But was part of them kind of proud that the government was using their numbers?
sentences.zh: 但他们当中是否有一部分人因为政府使用了他们的数字而感到有点自豪？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not sure how everyone on the project felt, but at least some of them were pretty shaken by this realization, like Aaron.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不确定项目中每个人的感受，但至少其中一些人对这一发现感到相当震惊，比如亚伦。

sentences.en: That's an immensely stressful position to be in for a bunch of volunteers, because on one hand, yeah, it's great that our numbers are actually really useful.
sentences.zh: 对于一群志愿者来说，这是一个极其有压力的位置，因为一方面，是的，我们的数据确实非常有用，这很棒。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, are you kidding me?
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你在开玩笑吗？

sentences.en: That's the best you can do with the entire resources of the federal government is get the data that we make every day by looking at websites.
sentences.zh: 动用整个联邦政府的资源，你所能做到的最好的事情，就是获取我们每天通过浏览网站制作出来的数据？

sentences.en: I mean, it's really hard for me to understand at this point, like, what was going on at the CDC.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，此时此刻我真的很难理解，疾病控制与预防中心当时到底在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: Like, what is going on within the agency at this time?
sentences.zh: 就像，这个机构当时内部到底在发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'll start by saying that we came into the pandemic with data systems that just were not designed to gather and process the kind of fast,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我首先要说的是，我们进入这场大流行时，所使用的数据系统根本不是为了收集和处理那种快速、

sentences.en: high-resolution data that people wanted.
sentences.zh: 高分辨率的数据而设计的，而这正是人们想要的。

sentences.en: Like, the demand for data just went way beyond what public health officials had ever encountered before, and they were caught flat-footed.
sentences.zh: 就像，对数据的需求远远超出了公共卫生官员以往遇到过的任何情况，他们被打了个措手不及。

sentences.en: There was also the general organizational chaos of the Trump administration, which certainly didn't help.
sentences.zh: 当时还存在特朗普政府普遍的组织混乱，这当然也无济于事。

sentences.en: But there were a number of ways the CDC tried to compensate.
sentences.zh: 但疾病控制与预防中心尝试通过多种方式进行弥补。

sentences.en: So, as an example, in April 2020, the agency started working on a new electronic reporting system that would collect detailed testing data from every state.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，在 2020 年 4 月，该机构开始着手开发一个新的电子报告系统，用于收集来自各州的详细测试数据。

sentences.en: It took a long time to get all the states onboarded to that system, like, more than a year.
sentences.zh: 让所有州都接入该系统花费了很长时间，比如一年多。

sentences.en: As that was happening, the agency was also using some of its existing surveillance systems and methods to track this new disease.
sentences.zh: 在进行这项工作的同时，该机构还利用其现有的部分监测系统和方法来追踪这种新疾病。

sentences.en: Finally, CDC quietly launched a new website.
sentences.zh: 最后，疾病控制与预防中心悄悄推出了一个新网站。

sentences.en: So, for example, this is another press conference held by the Coronavirus Task Force in early April, where they talk about data that the CDC has started to release.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，这是冠状病毒工作组在 4 月初举行的另一场新闻发布会，他们在会上讨论了疾病控制与预防中心开始发布的数据。

sentences.en: This surveillance data is bringing together our influenza-like illnesses with their syndromic management databases so that you can track...
sentences.zh: 这些监测数据将我们的流感样疾病与他们的综合管理数据库结合起来，以便你可以追踪……

sentences.en: And just to parse that for you...
sentences.zh: 为了给你们剖析一下……

sentences.en: Yeah, that would be helpful.
sentences.zh: 好的，那会很有帮助。

sentences.en: So, what they were doing is that the agency had adapted a couple of their existing systems for this new task of tracking COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们当时在做的是，该机构调整了他们现有的几个系统，以适应追踪新冠这一新任务。

sentences.en: Their system that tracks unusual levels of disease in places like emergency rooms and urgent care centers.
sentences.zh: 他们的系统用于追踪急诊室和紧急护理中心等地方的不寻常疾病水平。

sentences.en: That's the syndromic surveillance data.
sentences.zh: 这就是综合监测数据。

sentences.en: And their flu reporting systeMs.
sentences.zh: 以及他们的流感报告系统。

sentences.en: And the way that the CDC tracks flu is that they sample the population and then model a broader picture.
sentences.zh: 疾病控制与预防中心追踪流感的方法是，他们对人口进行抽样，然后建模出一个更广泛的画面。

sentences.en: So, the data isn't comprehensive.
sentences.zh: 所以这些数据并不全面。

sentences.en: And there are definitely some reasons for using the older system.
sentences.zh: 使用旧系统确实有一些原因。

sentences.en: For one thing, the states were already used to it.
sentences.zh: 首先，各州已经习惯了它。

sentences.en: But the United States, the states are used to using this system.
sentences.zh: 但美国，各州已经习惯使用这个系统了。

sentences.en: It's in emergency rooMs.
sentences.zh: 它在急诊室里。

sentences.en: It's in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 它在医院里。

sentences.en: It's in doctor's offices.
sentences.zh: 它在医生办公室里。

sentences.en: And it gives you insight and you can see very...
sentences.zh: 它能让你获得洞察，并且你可以非常清楚地看到……

sentences.en: But the fact was, these existing systems just weren't working that well.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，这些现有的系统就是运作得不是很好。

sentences.en: The agency was struggling to keep track of testing and case rates across the country.
sentences.zh: 该机构一直在努力追踪全国各地的检测和病例发生率。

sentences.en: It was struggling to update hospital data, which includes really critical stuff like bed availability and ventilator supply.
sentences.zh: 它一直在努力更新医院数据，其中包括真正关键的内容，比如床位可用性和呼吸机供应情况。

sentences.en: And with the hospital data, this is like a whole other story.
sentences.zh: 至于医院数据，这简直是另一个故事了。

sentences.en: But the CDC was moving so slowly that eventually the agency that oversees them, HHS, just took over gathering those stats and built a much better and faster system.
sentences.zh: 但疾病控制与预防中心的行动太慢了，以至于最终监管他们的机构——卫生与公众服务部，直接接管了这些统计数据的收集，并构建了一个更好、更快的系统。

sentences.en: But the CDC still seems to be at the center of all this today.
sentences.zh: 但直到今天，疾病控制与预防中心似乎仍然处于这一切的中心。

sentences.en: So, does that mean that they eventually started gathering those stats themselves in a different way or updated their systems?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是否意味着他们最终以另一种方式开始自己收集这些统计数据或者更新了他们的系统？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They eventually pivoted.
sentences.zh: 他们最终转变了方向。

sentences.en: But it took months before they started aggregating and sharing more of their own data.
sentences.zh: 但他们花了几个月的时间才开始汇总和分享更多他们自己的数据。

sentences.en: So, they released their own data tracker in early May, which was 15 weeks after the first reported case of COVID in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在 5 月初发布了自己的数据追踪器，这距离美国首例报告的新冠病例有 15 周之久，

sentences.en: and more than eight weeks after the launch of the COVID tracking project.
sentences.zh: 并且距离新冠追踪项目启动已经过去了八周多。

sentences.en: And even when they did that, there continued to be problems with the data and big discrepancies between their testing numbers and state numbers.
sentences.zh: 即便他们这样做了，数据仍然不断出现问题，他们的检测数字与各州的数字之间也存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: And is there a sense of why it would take so long?
sentences.zh: 大家对为什么会花费这么长时间有什么看法吗？

sentences.en: I mean, like a few enterprising journalists and a bunch of volunteers had something very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几个足智多谋的记者和一群志愿者很快就搞出了一些东西。

sentences.en: Why do you think it took the CDC so long?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么疾病控制与预防中心花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: Well, I have reached out to the CDC a number of times to try and get their take on all this, and they haven't responded.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我曾多次联系疾病控制与预防中心，试图了解他们对这一切的看法，但他们没有回应。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of critics of the CDC think there is something in the structure and culture of the agency that keeps them from moving fast and breaking protocol in an emergency.
sentences.zh: 但我认为许多疾病控制与预防中心的批评者认为，该机构的结构和文化中存在某种东西，阻碍了他们在紧急情况下迅速行动和打破常规。

sentences.en: You know, I think there was an attitude among a lot of people in the CDC about not overreacting to COVID.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为疾病控制与预防中心许多人有一种态度，即不要对新冠过度反应。

sentences.en: Basically like, oh, well, you know, if we design all these systems around the disease du jour,
sentences.zh: 基本上就像，哦，好吧，你知道的，如果我们围绕当下的流行病设计所有这些系统，

sentences.en: they even have like a comment like this on the CDC's data modernization page for one of like the conferences they had.
sentences.zh: 他们在疾病控制与预防中心的数据现代化页面上甚至有这样一条评论，是关于他们举办的某个会议的。

sentences.en: You know, basically like quoting someone at the conference saying like, we can't like over respond to the disease du jour.
sentences.zh: 你知道，基本上就像引用会议上某人的话说，我们不能对当下的流行病过度反应。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 而我的感觉是，哦，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Did your other diseases du jours kill 600,000 people?
sentences.zh: 你们以前遇到的那些当下的流行病杀死了 60 万人吗？

sentences.en: Like it's closer to a million now.
sentences.zh: 现在这个数字更接近一百万了。

sentences.en: Maybe we should be overreacting to this one.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该对这个反应过度一点。

sentences.en: Seems seems reasonable to design things around this, you know.
sentences.zh: 围绕这个来设计系统似乎，你知道的，挺合理的。

sentences.en: And I think that that was really a big piece of it was like they didn't want to custom design systems just for COVID.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实是很大一部分原因，那就是他们不想专门为新冠定制设计系统。

sentences.en: That was not what the CDC wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 那不是疾病控制与预防中心想做的事。

sentences.en: But in an unprecedented situation with a new disease we had never encountered before,
sentences.zh: 但在面对前所未有的情况时，这种新疾病是我们从未遇到过的，

sentences.en: moving through the population in ways that we were only beginning to understand,
sentences.zh: 它在人群中传播的方式是我们才刚刚开始了解的，

sentences.en: we needed new systems and we needed the public health establishment to be as deep in the data as the COVID tracking project was.
sentences.zh: 我们需要新的系统，我们需要公共卫生机构像COVID追踪项目那样深入掌握数据。

sentences.en: If you're not in the data every day or every few days, if you don't know how it's constructed,
sentences.zh: 如果你不是每天或每隔几天就看一次数据，如果你不知道它是如何构建的，

sentences.en: you don't understand what's actually happening and like where the future hotspots are and the future places to be concerned.
sentences.zh: 你就不会真正理解正在发生的事情，也不会知道未来的热点在哪里、哪些地方需要关注。

sentences.en: And you don't understand what it looks like when a state explodes with cases.
sentences.zh: 而且你也不会明白当一个州的病例激增时是什么样的情形。

sentences.en: So I know the COVID tracking project no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道COVID追踪项目已经不存在了。

sentences.en: So how did they make that decision to end the project?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是如何做出结束该项目的决定的呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, about a year into the pandemic, as Biden was coming into office,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，在大流行大约一年后，随着拜登政府上台，

sentences.en: you know, vaccinations were happening and the pandemic seemed to be on the wane.
sentences.zh: 你知道，疫苗接种正在进行，大流行似乎也在消退。

sentences.en: And so that was when they stopped it.
sentences.zh: 所以也就是在那时他们停下了项目。

sentences.en: And part of it was that it was taking a toll on the people involved.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为这对参与其中的人造成了沉重的负担。

sentences.en: Like they had never intended it to be a long-term project.
sentences.zh: 比如他们从来没有打算把它作为一个长期项目。

sentences.en: And even something as mundane as data entry had a high coSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至连数据录入这样平凡的事情也有很高的代价。

sentences.en: While this was happening, we had family members dying.
sentences.zh: 正当这一切发生时，我们的亲人却在离去。

sentences.en: We had people we knew who were in those statistics.
sentences.zh: 我们认识的人也成了那些统计数字的一部分。

sentences.en: But there was another reason as well, which is that the COVID tracking project founders really thought the government should be responsible for this work.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个原因，那就是COVID追踪项目的创立者们真的认为政府应该负责这项工作。

sentences.en: You know, we did not think that the public health data in widest distribution for the United States and the COVID pandemic should come from volunteer labor.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们认为美国和COVID大流行中最广泛分发的公共卫生数据不应该来自志愿者的劳动力。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration had promised to create a pandemic dashboard, which the COVID tracking project people were excited about.
sentences.zh: 而拜登政府曾承诺创建一个大流行仪表盘，这让COVID追踪项目的人感到很兴奋。

sentences.en: They even helped advise on a framework for how to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至协助就如何做到这一点的框架提出了建议。

sentences.en: But now, more than a year into Biden's term, that still has not materialized.
sentences.zh: 但现在，在拜登任期过了一年多之后，这个承诺仍未实现。

sentences.en: Even though COVID-related data remains both very critical and quite confusing to understand.
sentences.zh: 尽管与COVID相关的数据依然非常关键，而且相当令人迷惑不解。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: what made the COVID tracking project unique as an organization was that they were dedicated to researching and explaining all these various flaws and inconsistencies in the data.
sentences.zh: 作为一个组织，COVID追踪项目的独特之处在于，他们致力于研究和解释数据中的所有这些各种缺陷和不一致之处。

sentences.en: There were other data trackers and other volunteer data groups, but it was the COVID tracking project that was really dedicated to that kind of analysis, which we still badly need.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的数据追踪器和其他的志愿者数据小组，但正是COVID追踪项目真正致力于这种分析，而我们现在依然非常需要这种分析。

sentences.en: Data can't talk.
sentences.zh: 数据是不会说话的。

sentences.en: Data can't explain itself, particularly when you're speaking either to, you know, this idea of a general public, but also to reporters, to anybody in media,
sentences.zh: 数据无法自我解释，特别是当你面对的不仅是公众这种概念，还有记者、任何媒体从业人员，

sentences.en: to people even in government agencies.
sentences.zh: 甚至包括政府机构里的人时。

sentences.en: The data has to be contextualized and explained, and that's still largely not happening.
sentences.zh: 数据必须被赋予上下文并加以解释，而这在很大程度上仍然没有发生。

sentences.en: I should say, all the folks I spoke with at the COVID tracking project recognize that there are some things the CDC does really, really well.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我在COVID追踪项目交谈过的所有人，都承认疾控中心确实有些事情做得非常非常棒。

sentences.en: There are incredible scientists at CDC and NIH doing this remarkable, world-changing work on vaccines and all of these other things.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心和国立卫生研究院有不可思议的科学家们，在疫苗和所有这些其他方面从事着这种卓越的、改变世界的工作。

sentences.en: And the CDC did have some successes with data as well.
sentences.zh: 而且疾控中心在数据方面也确实取得了一些成功。

sentences.en: You know, the electronic lab reporting system the agency helped build has apparently really increased the speed and accuracy of state data coming into the agency.
sentences.zh: 你知道，该机构协助建立的电子实验室报告系统，显然确实提高了州数据进入该机构的速度和准确性。

sentences.en: But we're still nowhere near having the kind of surveillance systems we'll need the next time a pandemic happens.
sentences.zh: 但我们离拥有下一次大流行时所需要的监视系统还差得很远。

sentences.en: If you talk to pandemic people, you know, like, this was like a starter pandemic.
sentences.zh: 如果你和研究大流行的人谈谈，你知道的，就像，这只是一场入门级的大流行。

sentences.en: I mean, it just could have been so much worse, and it will be so much worse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它本可能糟糕得多，而且未来也将会糟糕得多。

sentences.en: You know, we know we are going to face worse threats.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们知道我们将面临更糟糕的威胁。

sentences.en: And the thing that I have never seen is any real reckoning in the federal government with what we didn't do, with the failures to build a real surveillance system.
sentences.zh: 而我从来没有见过的，是联邦政府对我们没有做的事情、对未能建立真正监视系统的失败进行任何真正的清算。

sentences.en: While I was working on this story, I ended up thinking a lot about this thing that Stephen Johnson told me.
sentences.zh: 在我做这篇报道的时候，我最终一直在思考斯蒂芬·约翰逊告诉我的一件事。

sentences.en: He was one of the historians of public health.
sentences.zh: 他是公共卫生历史学家之一。

sentences.en: I asked him if he had followed the work of the COVID tracking project and what he made of it.
sentences.zh: 我问他是否关注过COVID追踪项目的工作，以及他是如何看待的。

sentences.en: I had two reactions in a way to the COVID data project, which was, on the one hand, it seemed scandalous that they had to do the work that they had to do,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我对COVID数据项目有两种反应，一方面，他们不得不去做他们不得不做的那种工作，这似乎是一场丑闻，

sentences.en: that that should have already been underway.
sentences.zh: 那些工作本应该已经展开了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: That's my reaction, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是我的反应。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, too, there was part of me that was like, OK, these are the heirs to John Gronk,
sentences.zh: 但同时，我内心的一部分想法是，好吧，这些是约翰·格朗克的传人，

sentences.en: the amateur data collector who does it because they perceive something is missing in the system and there's not a lot of time to lose and they need to get in there and fill in this missing piece.
sentences.zh: 那个业余的数据收集者，他们这样做是因为他们察觉到系统里缺少了某些东西，而且时间紧迫，他们需要介入并填补这个缺失的部分。

sentences.en: That's a beautiful tradition in the history of health.
sentences.zh: 这是健康史上一项美丽的传统。

sentences.en: And so part of me was kind of moved to see it kick into gear.
sentences.zh: 所以我的内心有一部分被它启动时的情景触动了。

sentences.en: I mean, I get that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我懂这个。

sentences.en: I love that story.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: And I'm struck by the fact that John Gronk is a romantic figure of a person jumping in and filling in a need and inventing whole new fields of science at the same time.
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的是，约翰·格朗克是一个具有浪漫色彩的人物，他挺身而出填补需求，同时还在开创全新的科学领域。

sentences.en: But, you know, the story of the COVID tracking project, I'm really impressed by the people who did it.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，COVID追踪项目的故事，我对那些做这件事的人深表钦佩。

sentences.en: But it doesn't seem like a romantic story at all.
sentences.zh: 但它看起来一点也不像个浪漫的故事。

sentences.en: Like, it really feels like a tragedy to me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它真的很像一出悲剧。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I think it is a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 对，我想，我认为这是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: Like, we shouldn't have to John Gronk the pandemic, not after hundreds of years of public health developments.
sentences.zh: 就像，在经历了数百年的公共卫生发展之后，我们本不该用约翰·格朗克的方式来应对大流行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, what we really want is a boring story where a bureaucracy just does its job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们真正想要的是一个无聊的故事，即官僚机构只是在做好它的本职工作。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, competent bureaucrats.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，称职的官僚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Here's to the competent bureaucrats.
sentences.zh: 向称职的官僚致敬。

sentences.en: Coming up next, we'll talk about some potential fixes for our public health data systeMs.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将讨论修复公共卫生数据系统的一些潜在方案。

sentences.en: We'll hear from a former CDC director and someone who has thought a lot about who gets erased from our current data and how to make it better.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到一位前疾控中心主任的发言，以及一位深入思考过谁在当前数据中被抹去以及如何改善现状的人的观点。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Support for this four part series exploring the future of health and well-being comes from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation,
sentences.zh: 本期探讨健康与福祉未来的四集系列节目得到了罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会的支持，

sentences.en: which is committed to improving health and health equity in the United States.
sentences.zh: 该基金会致力于改善美国的健康和健康公平。

sentences.en: Knowing that the healthy, equitable future we all deserve won't simply arrive,
sentences.zh: 深知我们应得的健康、公平的未来不会凭空降临，

sentences.en: RWJF is exploring how new technologies, scientific discoveries, cultural shifts, and unforeseen events like those in today's story may shape our lives in years to come.
sentences.zh: RWJF 正在探索诸如今天故事中的新技术、科学发现、文化转变和突发事件将如何塑造我们未来的生活。

sentences.en: Through these explorations, they're learning what it will take to build a future that provides every individual with a fair and just opportunity to thrive no matter who they are,
sentences.zh: 通过这些探索，他们正在了解需要做什么，才能建立一个无论人们是谁、

sentences.en: where they live, or how much money they make.
sentences.zh: 住在哪里、赚多少钱，都能为每个人提供公平公正的发展机会的未来。

sentences.en: Learn more about their efforts at RWJF.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问 RWJF.org 了解更多关于他们工作的信息。

sentences.en: And if you like thinking about the future of things and have a hunch about the future, share it at shareyourhunch.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢思考事物的未来并且对未来有直觉，请在 shareyourhunch.org 上分享它。

sentences.en: I'm going there now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就去那儿。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm selecting the prompt, I have a hunch.
sentences.zh: 好的，我正在选择提示，我有一种直觉。

sentences.en: I have a hunch that the increasing misery of air travel will cause people to reconsider train travel in the U.S., and it will be more popular than it has been for decades.
sentences.zh: 我有一种直觉，航空旅行日益增长的痛苦将促使人们重新考虑美国的火车旅行，它的受欢迎程度将超过几十年来水平。

sentences.en: Check out other hunches and share your own hunch at shareyourhunch.org.
sentences.zh: 去 shareyourhunch.org 查看其他人的直觉并分享你自己的直觉吧。

sentences.en: All right, I'm back with Delaney Hall, and we're going to be talking about how to fix our public health surveillance systems,
sentences.zh: 好的，我回到了黛兰妮·霍尔这里，我们要讨论的是如何修复我们的公共卫生监视系统，

sentences.en: which that sounds really ominous when I say it that way, but that's really what we're trying to fix.
sentences.zh: 我这么说听起来可能真的很不祥，但这确实是我们试图修复的目标。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is the good kind of surveillance system.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是那种好的监视系统。

sentences.en: This is the surveillance that we want.
sentences.zh: 这是我们想要的监视。

sentences.en: So how do we fix them?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何修复它们呢？

sentences.en: I guess, you know, spoiler alert, I don't think there is one clear answer to that massive problem.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，剧透一下，对于这个巨大的问题，我认为并没有一个明确的答案。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can't say I'm surprised to hear that.
sentences.zh: 是的，听到这个我可不觉得意外。

sentences.en: But I did speak with people during my reporting who had a range of interesting ideas about how to make things work better, both within the system and with data in particular,
sentences.zh: 但在我的报道过程中，我确实与一些人交谈过，他们对如何让事情运作得更好有一系列有趣的看法，无论是在系统内部还是在数据方面，

sentences.en: and especially with race and ethnicity data, which represents one of the biggest failures in our current system.
sentences.zh: 尤其是种族和族裔数据，这代表了我们当前系统中的最大失败之一。

sentences.en: Oh, that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me more about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，请多告诉我一些这方面的情况。

sentences.en: So I will get to the race and ethnicity data a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 所以我稍后会讲到种族和族裔数据。

sentences.en: I wanted to start with one immediate fix that came up in conversation with Alexis Madrigal of the COVID Tracking Project.
sentences.zh: 我想从与COVID追踪项目的亚历克西斯·马德里加尔的对话中提出的一个直接修复方案开始。
zh_words: 亚历克西斯·马德里加尔

sentences.en: And he said it really would have helped if the federal government had just been extremely clear with states about what information they wanted reported and how,
sentences.zh: 他说，如果联邦政府能非常明确地告诉各州他们希望报告什么信息以及如何报告，那将真的很有帮助，

sentences.en: because then the data coming from the states would have been more standardized and easier to compare and analyze.
sentences.zh: 因为这样一来，各州提供的数据就会更加标准化，更容易进行比较和分析。

sentences.en: Probably the thing that would have made the biggest single difference on a data level would be if the federal government had said basically on an ultra, ultra,
sentences.zh: 可能在数据层面上会带来最大单一改变的事情，就是如果联邦政府基本上以一种超级、超级、

sentences.en: ultra precise level is what we need.
sentences.zh: 超级精确的水平说这就是我们需要的东西。

sentences.en: Like we need it to come like from this system and answer all those small questions.
sentences.zh: 就像我们需要它来自这个系统并回答所有这些小问题一样。

sentences.en: And this was actually something that the COVID Tracking Project ended up doing in the absence of really clear guidance from the government.
sentences.zh: 而在政府缺乏真正明确指导的情况下，这实际上正是COVID追踪项目最终所做的事情。

sentences.en: They pulled together their own guidelines and distributed them to the states.
sentences.zh: 他们整理出了自己的指南并分发给了各州。

sentences.en: Oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很有趣。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing that if that guidance was coming, you know, straight from the government, it would probably be more successful.
sentences.zh: 但我猜，如果这些指导方针是直接来自政府的话，可能会取得更大的成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the government, believe it or not, has more authority than a volunteer effort, however impressive that effort was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管你信不信，政府比志愿者工作拥有更大的权威，无论那个志愿者工作有多么令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: The other thing is, even if the government had been really clear about how it wanted the data reported, that would have made things better for sure.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，即使政府对它希望如何报告数据非常明确，那当然也会让事情变得更好。

sentences.en: But it wouldn't have solved the underlying issues with the surveillance system.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能解决监视系统的根本问题。

sentences.en: Those are much bigger and more complex.
sentences.zh: 那些问题要大得多，也复杂得多。

sentences.en: You can't fix the data system without fixing the broader public health system.
sentences.zh: 不修复更广泛的公共卫生系统，你就无法修复数据系统。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Thomas Frieden.
sentences.zh: 这位是托马斯·弗里登博士。

sentences.en: He was the director of the CDC from 2009 to 2017.
sentences.zh: 他在2009年至2017年期间担任疾控中心主任。

sentences.en: He also worked as the health commissioner for New York City for seven years.
sentences.zh: 他还担任了七年纽约市卫生专员。

sentences.en: And he testified before Congress in March 2021.
sentences.zh: 他在2021年3月向国会作证。

sentences.en: So this was around the time the COVID Tracking Project shut down.
sentences.zh: 所以这大约是在COVID追踪项目关闭的时候。

sentences.en: And he said in that testimony that, quote, lack of accurate real-time information was one of the greatest failures of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他在证词中表示，引述一下，缺乏准确的实时信息是美国

sentences.en: response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 应对COVID-19大流行最大的失败之一。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: OK, that's definitive.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很绝对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he said that our data systems are broken, basically, from the top to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说我们的数据系统从上到下基本上都崩溃了。

sentences.en: And he said that it is not just the CDC's fault here.
sentences.zh: 并且他说这并不仅仅是疾控中心的过错。

sentences.en: So I think saying, well, CDC couldn't get the data together, CDC was dealing with local and state health departments that were overwhelmed and couldn't collect the data,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果说，嗯，疾控中心无法将数据汇集起来，那是因为疾控中心应对的是不堪重负、无法收集数据的本地和州卫生部门，

sentences.en: hospitals that didn't have standardized data, and laboratory testing that was insufficient, and a contact tracing system that never really worked effectively in most places.
sentences.zh: 是没有标准化数据的医院，是不充分的实验室检测，以及在大多数地方从未真正有效运作过的接触者追踪系统。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a wide range of failures.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一系列广泛的失败。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I imagine this all goes back to both the fractured nature of our public health system and the way the states and the federal government really don't work hand-in-hand when it comes to these things.
sentences.zh: 我想这一切都可以追溯到我们公共卫生系统的破碎性，以及各州和联邦政府在这些事情上确实没有携手合作的方式。

sentences.en: And then we also talked about the hauling out of these institutions and systems that has been going on for decades, really.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还讨论了这些机构和系统几十年来的空壳化现象。

sentences.en: Our system got to this very bad point thanks to underfunding it for decades.
sentences.zh: 由于数十年来资金不足，我们的系统才走到了今天这个非常糟糕的地步。

sentences.en: And we talked about this a little bit in the piece, but we're already seeing the cycle of panic and neglect, as it's known, kick in yet again.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中稍微讨论过这一点，但正如人们所知的那样，我们已经看到这种恐慌与忽视的循环再次拉开序幕。

sentences.en: So a crisis happens, money and resources pour in, the crisis fades, and the money goes away.
sentences.zh: 所以危机发生，资金和资源涌入，危机消退，资金随之消失。

sentences.en: And this is just not a good way to fund a system that needs to rebuild some of its critical infrastructure from the bottom up.
sentences.zh: 而这绝对不是资助一个需要从底层重建部分关键基础设施的系统的好方法。

sentences.en: You can't build a sustainable system with one-time dollars.
sentences.zh: 你无法用一次性的资金来建立一个可持续的系统。

sentences.en: And he really wants to see us build that sustainable system.
sentences.zh: 他非常希望看到我们建立起那个可持续的系统。

sentences.en: He knows, everyone in public health knows, that this kind of real-time data collection is important.
sentences.zh: 他知道，公共卫生领域的每个人都知道，这种实时数据收集非常重要。

sentences.en: But Dr. Frieden says it's going to take years of investment to fix it.
sentences.zh: 但弗里登博士表示，修复它需要长达数年的投资。

sentences.en: You know, there needs to be an agreement about a national architecture for data gathering and sharing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，需要就数据收集和共享的国家架构达成一致。

sentences.en: The government needs to be able to hire really talented programmers.
sentences.zh: 政府需要能够聘请到真正有才华的程序员。

sentences.en: We need to find workarounds for some very tricky problems, including the fact that we don't have national health identifiers in this country,
sentences.zh: 我们需要为一些非常棘手的问题找到变通方案，包括我们在国内没有国家健康标识符这一事实，

sentences.en: which means that tracking people across different systems is a big challenge.
sentences.zh: 这意味着跨不同系统追踪人员是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: There's just, there's a lot to sort out.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，有很多事情需要理清。

sentences.en: We need a multi-year investment to modernize it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要多年的投资来使其现代化。

sentences.en: It's not just a matter of replacing fax machines with an electronic secure interchange.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是用电子安全交换系统替换传真机的问题。

sentences.en: But as we also heard in the main story, this is not just about money or technology.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在主干故事中所听到的，这不仅关乎金钱或技术。

sentences.en: Those things are definitely important.
sentences.zh: 这些东西当然很重要。

sentences.en: But there are elements of the CDC's current culture and how it interacts with local health departments that also needs to change.
sentences.zh: 但疾控中心当前文化及其与地方卫生部门互动的方式中，也有一些元素需要改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So my impression of the CDC is that it's a very, you know, scientific and academic organization in terms of its outlook.
sentences.zh: 所以我对疾控中心的印象是，从其视角来看，它是一个非常科学和学术化的组织。

sentences.en: Like, they do very careful analysis before they release anything or recommend anything.
sentences.zh: 比如，在发布任何内容或推荐任何事情之前，他们会做非常仔细的分析。

sentences.en: And that's not always what the public kind of demands.
sentences.zh: 而这并不总是公众所期望的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's safe to say that the agency tends to move slow.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以肯定地说，该机构的行动往往比较慢。

sentences.en: It's also, Frieden pointed out, sometimes subject to political oversight and vetting that can contribute to that slowness.
sentences.zh: 弗里登还指出，它有时还要服从政治监督和审查，这也会导致这种缓慢。

sentences.en: But for whatever reasons, I think it moves at a different pace than people in local health departments who are frontline responders.
sentences.zh: 但无论出于什么原因，我认为它的行动节奏与作为一线响应人员的地方卫生部门的人不同。

sentences.en: They need to move fast, sometimes with just the best data available at that moment.
sentences.zh: 他们需要快速行动，有时只能依靠那一刻掌握的最好的数据。

sentences.en: And so Frieden thinks there should be more movement back and forth between the CDC and local and state level health departments so they can understand each other's needs.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗里登认为疾控中心与地方及州级卫生部门之间应该有更多双向交流，以便他们能够理解彼此的需求。

sentences.en: There are too few people working at CDC headquarters in Atlanta who have worked for two or five or ten years at a county or city or state or global health department.
sentences.zh: 在亚特兰大疾控中心总部工作的人中，有很少一部分人曾在县、市、州或全球卫生部门工作过两年、五年或十年。

sentences.en: Embedded to understand that if you need an answer, sometimes it's in the next four or five minutes, not in the next four or five hours,
sentences.zh: 他们深入基层，明白当你需要一个答案时，有时它需要在接下来的四五分钟内得到，而不是在接下来的四五个小时内，

sentences.en: and certainly not in the next four or five days.
sentences.zh: 更不用说在接下来的四五天里了。

sentences.en: And so what Dr. Frieden has proposed is having thousands of staff on the CDC payroll who are actually embedded in county and city health departments for a few years and who then rotate back to CDC headquarters.
sentences.zh: 所以弗里登博士提出的建议是，让数千名疾控中心编制的员工实际深入到县市卫生部门工作几年，然后他们再轮岗回到疾控中心总部。

sentences.en: That's an interesting suggestion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的建议。

sentences.en: I mean, are there any indications that the CDC is seriously looking at this or changing its culture in any way?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有什么迹象表明疾控中心正在认真考虑这一点，或者在以任何方式改变其文化吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I have not heard of anything like what Dr. Frieden is proposing, like a cultural exchange between the CDC and local health departments.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我没有听说过任何类似于弗里登博士所提出的建议，比如疾控中心与地方卫生部门之间的文化交流。

sentences.en: I also think that the COVID tracking project founders would say there is nothing close to the level of soul searching that they would like to see happening at the CDC right now.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，COVID追踪项目的创立者会说，现在疾控中心内部发生的深刻反省，远没有达到他们希望看到的水平。

sentences.en: Like a real reckoning with what went wrong during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 就像是对大流行期间出现的问题进行真正的清算。

sentences.en: But, you know, there are some new efforts at the agency, like, for example, a center within the CDC called the Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics, the CFA.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，该机构有一些新的努力，比如，疾控中心内部成立了一个名为疾病预测与疫情分析中心（CFA）的机构。

sentences.en: So what's the CFA supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 那么CFA要做什么呢？

sentences.en: It's being billed as a weather service for disease, a group that can forecast outbreaks, which is interesting and challenging work.
sentences.zh: 它被称为疾病的气象局，一个能够预测疫情的团队，这是一项有趣且充满挑战的工作。

sentences.en: And how it relates to data is that the quality of any given model and its resulting forecast depends very heavily on the quality of data that goes into it.
sentences.zh: 它与数据的关系在于，任何给定模型的质量及其最终的预测很大程度上取决于输入其中的数据的质量。

sentences.en: So in our current system, where even simple metrics like test positivity rates or hospitalizations are ambiguous, that is going to be a problem for the pandemic modelers.
sentences.zh: 因此在我们目前的系统中，即使是像检测阳性率或住院人数这样简单的指标也是模棱两可的，这对大流行病建模人员来说将是一个问题。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: I mean, if the CFA is going to be successful,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果CFA想要成功，

sentences.en: they've got to sort out that data stuff from the get go because you could have the greatest model in the world and all these people willing to do it and they could predict amazing things.
sentences.zh: 他们必须从一开始就理顺这些数据问题，因为你可能拥有世界上最棒的模型，所有人也都愿意去做，而且他们可以预测出惊人的结果。

sentences.en: But if the data is not there, then it does not matter.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有数据，那就无济于事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The data stuff has to come firSt. It's foundational.
sentences.zh: 数据问题必须放在第一位。这是基础。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, if we're going to be rebuilding our data systems in the way that Frieden is describing, it's worth thinking through this question in particular.
sentences.zh: 就像我们要按照弗里登所描述的那样重建数据系统一样，特别值得深入思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I remember when I was following the work at the COVID Tracking Project, like this was an issue that they really focused on.
sentences.zh: 我记得当我关注COVID追踪项目的工作时，这确实是他们非常关注的一个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, it definitely was.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: The COVID Tracking Project ended up developing a whole wing of their project devoted specifically to race and ethnicity data.
sentences.zh: COVID追踪项目最终开发了他们项目的一个全新分支，专门致力于种族和族裔数据。

sentences.en: They did that work in collaboration with Dr. Ibram X.
sentences.zh: 他们与伊布拉姆·X·肯迪博士合作开展了这项工作，

sentences.en: Kendi, who runs the Boston University Center for Anti-Racist Research.
sentences.zh: 肯迪博士负责波士顿大学的反种族主义研究中心。

sentences.en: And early in the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 在大流行初期，

sentences.en: Dr. Kendi wrote a series of essays in The Atlantic where he argued that we really do not know who's being most impacted by COVID-19 because the data around race is just so limited.
sentences.zh: 肯迪博士在大西洋月刊上写了一系列文章，他在其中辩称，我们真的不知道谁受COVID-19的影响最大，因为关于种族的数据实在太有限了。

sentences.en: And so why is that?
sentences.zh: 那么这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Is it that race and ethnicity information is just not gathered?
sentences.zh: 是因为根本没有收集种族和族裔信息吗？

sentences.en: Is it just not shared?
sentences.zh: 是因为根本没有共享吗？

sentences.en: Like, what is the breakdown here?
sentences.zh: 这中间到底出了什么问题？

sentences.en: The data is insufficient in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 这些数据在很多方面都是不足的。

sentences.en: And to help explain how, I'd like to introduce you to Abigail Echo Hawk.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助解释具体是如何不足的，我想向大家介绍阿比盖尔·埃科·霍克。

sentences.en: We all know somebody.
sentences.zh: 我们都认识这样的人。

sentences.en: We all know somebody who is impacted by COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 我们都认识受COVID-19影响的人。

sentences.en: We all know somebody who is impacted by a death, even if we weren't ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们都认识受死亡影响的人，即使我们自己没有亲身经历。

sentences.en: Echo Hawk is a citizen of the Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma, and she's the director of the Urban Indian Health Institute in Seattle, Washington.
sentences.zh: 埃科·霍克是俄克拉荷马州波尼族的公民，她是华盛顿州西雅图城市印第安人卫生研究所的所长。

sentences.en: It's one of 12 tribal epidemiology centers in the country.
sentences.zh: 它是全国12个部落流行病学中心之一。

sentences.en: And Echo Hawk says that it's clear Native people were disproportionately affected by COVID, even just anecdotally.
sentences.zh: 埃科·霍克表示，从轶事中也很明显可以看出，原住民受疫情的影响是不成比例的严重。

sentences.en: Like she said, everybody knows somebody, but that it is impossible to know just how much.
sentences.zh: 就像她说的，每个人都认识这样的人，但却不可能知道程度究竟有多深。

sentences.en: Even when data was collected, they weren't collecting the race and ethnicity of American Indians, Alaska Natives, and many other people of color.
sentences.zh: 即使收集了数据，他们也没有收集美洲印第安人、阿拉斯加原住民以及许多其他有色人种的种族和族裔信息。

sentences.en: So while we know the impact on our people was great with the scarce data we had, we know it's a gross underreporting.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然我们知道根据手头稀少的数据，疫情对我们人民的影响是巨大的，但我们知道这被严重低报了。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is that the COVID pandemic has recently focused people's attention on this issue.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，COVID大流行最近将人们的注意力集中到了这个问题上。

sentences.en: Like this is something people are now talking about, the fact that the pandemic disproportionately affected people of color.
sentences.zh: 就像这是人们现在正在谈论的事情，即大流行对有色人种产生的不成比例的影响这一事实。

sentences.en: But Echo Hawk has been interested in the issue for much longer because ever since she started her career in public health,
sentences.zh: 但埃科·霍克对这个问题关注的时间要长得多，因为自从她开始公共卫生职业生涯以来，

sentences.en: she has seen the ways that Native people and other people of color are made invisible in the data.
sentences.zh: 她就看到了原住民和其他有色人种在数据中如何被隐形。

sentences.en: And it happens through a couple mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 这是通过几种机制发生的。

sentences.en: One is by virtue of being a small population that can be difficult to gather, quote, statistically significant data about.
sentences.zh: 其一是由于人口基数小，很难收集到所谓的具有统计学意义的数据。

sentences.en: And I would be in meeting after meeting after meeting where we would be a little asterisk down at the bottom that would say not statistically significant or not reported on.
sentences.zh: 我会参加一个又一个的会议，在那里我们只是底部的一个小星号，上面写着“不具统计学意义”或“未报告”。

sentences.en: And so what it was is we were invisible.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是说，我们被隐形了。

sentences.en: And we were invisible in conversations that policymakers were having.
sentences.zh: 我们在决策者进行的对话中被隐形了。

sentences.en: We were invisible when they were allocating resources.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们分配资源时被隐形了。

sentences.en: And what I saw was incredible health disparities and the deaths of my community members, of my family members as a direct result.
sentences.zh: 我看到的是难以置信的健康差距，以及作为直接后果的我的社区成员、我的家庭成员的死亡。

sentences.en: So that's one way the data around ethnicity is lacking.
sentences.zh: 所以这是族裔数据缺乏的一种方式。

sentences.en: Another thing that happens is that people will sometimes be given options on a form, like maybe black, white, and other.
sentences.zh: 另一种情况是，有时人们会在表格上得到选项，比如可能是黑人、白人和其他。

sentences.en: It's like a limited range.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个有限的范围。

sentences.en: And other might be the only option that applies.
sentences.zh: 而“其他”可能是唯一适用的选项。

sentences.en: So they check that box.
sentences.zh: 于是他们勾选了那个选项。

sentences.en: That could include Japanese people.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括日本裔。

sentences.en: It could include American Indians, Alaska Natives.
sentences.zh: 可能包括美洲印第安人、阿拉斯加原住民。

sentences.en: It could include other race or ethnicities.
sentences.zh: 可能包括其他人种或族裔。

sentences.en: And even when you fill that in, they never disaggregate it.
sentences.zh: 而且即使你填写了，他们也从不进行细分。

sentences.en: That means that they kind of put it all together and they just count that other.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们把所有这些都混在一起，然后简单地统称为“其他”。

sentences.en: What that does is it effectively hides what's happening to a particular population of people.
sentences.zh: 这样做实际上掩盖了特定人群身上正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And this issue of aggregation and disaggregation is important.
sentences.zh: 而这种聚合与细分的问题非常重要。

sentences.en: So disaggregating the data just means breaking the data down into smaller units or segments instead of bundling a bunch of it up together,
sentences.zh: 因此，细分数据只是意味着将数据分解为更小的单位或部分，而不是把一大堆数据捆绑在一起，

sentences.en: which is what happens in the other category.
sentences.zh: 而这正是“其他”类别中所发生的情况。

sentences.en: It also sometimes happens with people who are multiple races.
sentences.zh: 这种情况有时也会发生在多元种族的人身上。

sentences.en: Say somebody like my children, who are Mexican-American and also American-Indian, and they mark on a form Hispanic, they mark American-Indian,
sentences.zh: 比方说像我的孩子，他们既有墨西哥裔美国人血统，也有美洲印第安人血统，他们在表格上勾选了“西班牙裔”，勾选了“美洲印第安人”，

sentences.en: and they mark Filipino because they're also Filipino.
sentences.zh: 还勾选了“菲律宾裔”，因为他们也有菲律宾血统。

sentences.en: And when the data is calculated, instead, they put them into a category that says multi-race.
sentences.zh: 而当计算数据时，他们并没有这样做，而是把这些人归入一个名为“多元种族”的类别。

sentences.en: But they don't disaggregate it in a way that says they are both Hispanic, they are both Filipino, and they are also American-Indian and Alaska Native.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有以一种能够说明他们既是西班牙裔、既是菲律宾裔、同时也是美洲印第安人和阿拉斯加原住民的方式来进行细分。

sentences.en: I mean, anyone could look at this and know that multi-race is a meaningless category that probably doesn't yield very much information at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何人看到这一点都会明白，“多元种族”是一个毫无意义的类别，可能根本产生不了多少有价值的信息。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It is not a very useful category.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个很有用的类别。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is that these other broad categories that we use a lot, like Asian-American as an example, when that's used in public health data,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们经常使用的其他这些广泛类别，比如以“亚裔美国人”为例，当它被用于公共卫生数据时，

sentences.en: it hides the fact that Asian-Americans are an incredibly diverse group.
sentences.zh: 它掩盖了一个事实，即亚裔美国人是一个极其多元的群体。

sentences.en: With very diverse experiences related to health and illness.
sentences.zh: 他们有着与健康和疾病相关的极其多元的经历。

sentences.en: Finally, Echo Hawk described yet another way that people of color get erased from the data, which is racial misclassification.
sentences.zh: 最后，埃科·霍克描述了有色人种从数据中被抹去的另一种方式，那就是种族错误分类。

sentences.en: Racial misclassification is when you go in and instead of asking you what race or ethnicity you are, somebody might look at you and instead check white based on visual appearance.
sentences.zh: 种族错误分类是指，当他们去收集数据时，没有询问你的种族或族裔，而是有人看了你一眼，然后根据你的外表勾选了“白人”。

sentences.en: Check black based on visual appearance.
sentences.zh: 根据外表勾选“黑人”。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So she means that whoever is filling out the form doesn't even ask.
sentences.zh: 所以她的意思是，填表的人甚至根本不问。

sentences.en: They just make an assumption based on appearance and they just fill it in.
sentences.zh: 他们只是根据外表进行主观推测，然后直接填上去。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And Echo Hawk says it happens all the time and it disproportionately hurts people of color by making the data around their existence and their health issues just fuzzy and incomplete.
sentences.zh: 埃科·霍克说这种情况时常发生，它通过使关于有色人种生存状况和健康问题的数据变得模糊和不完整，从而对有色人种造成了不成比例的伤害。

sentences.en: So does Echo Hawk have ideas about how to change the way we collect data so this type of stuff doesn't happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，埃科·霍克对于如何改变我们收集数据的方式有什么看法，好让这种事情不再发生吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, she does.
sentences.zh: 是的，她有。

sentences.en: She talks about decolonizing data and in addition to basic stuff like disaggregating data and allowing for greater nuance in race and ethnicity categories,
sentences.zh: 她谈到了数据的去殖民化，除了像细分数据以及允许在种族和族裔类别中有更多细微差别这样基础的事情之外，

sentences.en: she wants to see communities be more involved in deciding what gets gathered and shared about them.
sentences.zh: 她希望看到社区更多地参与决定收集和分享关于他们的哪些信息。

sentences.en: So she talks about how there's a deficit based framework in public health, where in the case of her community, the data always shows high rates of obesity, high rates of diabetes,
sentences.zh: 所以她谈到了公共卫生领域中存在的一种基于赤字的框架，以她的社区为例，数据总是显示高肥胖率、高糖尿病率，

sentences.en: you know, health challenges.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，各种健康挑战。

sentences.en: But she also sees a lot of strengths in her community, strengths that can actually measurably improve health.
sentences.zh: 但她也在自己的社区中看到了许多优势，这些优势实际上可以切实改善健康状况。

sentences.en: And so she'd like to see data gathered around that, too.
sentences.zh: 因此，她也希望围绕这些方面收集数据。

sentences.en: Yes, we need to know the gaps, but we also need to know how do our youth see themselves in the future?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们需要了解差距，但我们也需要了解我们的年轻人如何看待自己的未来？

sentences.en: If you can see yourself in the future, that's a protective factor against suicidality.
sentences.zh: 如果你能看到自己的未来，这就是抵御自杀倾向的一个保护因素。

sentences.en: We also want to know where their cultural ties are.
sentences.zh: 我们还想了解他们的文化纽带在哪里。

sentences.en: Are they culturally engaged?
sentences.zh: 他们是否积极参与文化活动？

sentences.en: Do they have the access to the resources for their cultural engagement?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有渠道获得进行文化活动所需的资源？

sentences.en: We want to use the strengths of our community, our cultural protective factors.
sentences.zh: 我们希望利用我们社区的优势、我们的文化保护因素。

sentences.en: All of those things are things that can be measured and they can be weighted against the gaps.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是可以被测量的事物，并且它们可以与各种差距进行权衡。

sentences.en: And her bigger point is just that data should serve the community and the needs of the community.
sentences.zh: 她更核心的观点是，数据应该服务于社区以及社区的需求。

sentences.en: It shouldn't just be to study the community and write academic papers about it.
sentences.zh: 它不应该仅仅用于研究社区并撰写相关的学术论文。

sentences.en: It should be actionable and lead to better health for the communities it comes from.
sentences.zh: 它应该是可采取行动的，并为其所源自的社区带来更好的健康状况。
